title: Microsoft FY2026 Annual Report - Letter to Shareholders
section: Building the Frontier Ecosystem / Letter to Shareholders
text:
Building the Frontier Ecosystem
Dear shareholders, colleagues, customers, and partners:
For Microsoft, the central question as we enter this Super Intelligence era is not just how big the opportunity becomes, but how we deliver the real-world outcomes that every country, community, and company demands and deserves.
After all, Super Intelligence is changing every organization's inputs (how they work) as well as their outputs (the products and services they sell). As a result, customers will increasingly measure the cost of tokens against the outcomes they produce. We call this the 'cost-to-outcome' frontier, and we are focused on optimizing it.
Fiscal year 2026 was another record year for the company. Revenue was $331.8 billion, up 18 percent year-over-year. Microsoft Cloud revenue was $214.4 billion, up 27 percent year-over-year. Azure grew 41 percent year-over-year and surpassed $100 billion for the first time, while Microsoft 365 Copilot reached over 30 million paid seats. And operating income was $155.2 billion, up 21 percent year-over-year.
In software development, GitHub Copilot now has 50 million users, and we worked to scale the platform to meet unprecedented demand.
Underlying all this is a new multimodel system where the harness—including context, memory, and action space—is separate from the model. This architecture optimizes the cost-to-outcome frontier by allowing us to use the right model for the right job, and strengthens business continuity and resilience because models become interchangeable.
We offer more than 11,000 models from OpenAI, Anthropic, Mistral, and others, as well as our own MAI family. Microsoft Foundry surpassed 100,000 customers. Work IQ context engine spans more than 17 exabytes of data. First-party silicon includes Maia 300 (40 percent more tokens per watt) and Cobalt 200 (over 50 percent higher performance).
Satya Nadella, Chairman and Chief Executive Officer, October 14, 2026.

Share Repurchases
On September 14, 2021, our Board of Directors approved a share repurchase program authorizing up to $60.0 billion in share repurchases. This program commenced in November 2021 and was completed in April 2025.

title: Microsoft FY2026 Annual Report - Business Overview & Reportable Segments
section: Business - General and Operating Segments
text:
BUSINESS - GENERAL
Founded in 1975, Microsoft is a technology company committed to making digital technology and artificial intelligence ('AI') available broadly and doing so responsibly. Our mission is to empower every person and every organization on the planet to achieve more.

OPERATING SEGMENTS
We operate our business and report our financial performance using three segments:
1. Productivity and Business Processes
Consists of Microsoft 365 Commercial products and cloud services (Office 365, Teams, Microsoft 365 Copilot), Microsoft 365 Consumer products and cloud services, LinkedIn (Talent, Marketing, Premium, Sales Solutions), and Dynamics products and cloud services (Dynamics 365, Power Apps, Power Automate).
2. Intelligent Cloud
Consists of public, private, and hybrid server products and cloud services. Comprises Server products and cloud services (Azure and other cloud services, GitHub, Health and Life Sciences cloud services formerly Nuance Healthcare cloud services, SQL Server, Windows Server) and Enterprise and partner services.
3. More Personal Computing
Consists of products and services that put customers at the center of the experience: Windows and Devices (Windows OEM licensing and Surface devices), XBOX (formerly Gaming, including first-party content, consoles, and XBOX Game Pass subscriptions), and Search advertising (Bing, Microsoft Copilot, Edge, and advertising affiliates).

title: Microsoft FY2026 Annual Report - Human Capital, Operations & R&D
section: Human Capital Resources and Operations
text:
HUMAN CAPITAL RESOURCES
As of June 30, 2026, we employed approximately 223,000 people on a full-time basis, 121,000 in the U.S. and 102,000 internationally.
By functional division:
- 89,000 employees were in operations, including product support, consulting services, datacenter operations, and manufacturing/distribution;
- 77,000 employees were in product research and development (R&D);
- 43,000 employees were in sales and marketing;
- 14,000 employees were in general and administration.

OPERATIONS AND R&D
We operate global operations service centers covering the Americas, Asia Pacific, Europe, and Middle East. We operate datacenters globally to meet growing AI and cloud computing demand.
We make significant investments in research and development internally. Software development costs are expensed until technological feasibility is reached shortly before production release.

title: Microsoft FY2026 Annual Report - MD&A Overview & Segment Results
section: MD&A - Summary Results of Operations & Segment Results
text:
MANAGEMENT'S DISCUSSION AND ANALYSIS (MD&A)
Highlights from fiscal year 2026 compared with fiscal year 2025:
- Microsoft Cloud revenue increased 27% to $214.4 billion.
- Commercial remaining performance obligation increased 84% to $678 billion.
- Metrics Update: In the first quarter of fiscal year 2026, Microsoft made updates to its metrics to align with how management monitors and manages certain businesses, and Microsoft 365 Consumer subscribers was removed as a metric.
- Microsoft Cloud gross margin percentage decreased to 66% driven by continued investments in AI infrastructure and growing AI product usage, offset in part by efficiency gains in Azure and Microsoft 365 Commercial cloud.

SUMMARY RESULTS OF OPERATIONS (in millions, except per share):
- Total revenue: $331,839 in FY26 compared to $281,724 in FY25 (18% growth).
- Gross margin: $225,465 in FY26 compared to $193,893 in FY25 (16% growth).
- Operating income: $155,237 in FY26 compared to $128,528 in FY25 (21% growth).
- Net income: $133,749 in FY26 compared to $101,832 in FY25 (31% growth).
- Diluted earnings per share (EPS): $17.95 in FY26 compared to $13.64 in FY25 (32% growth).
- Adjusted diluted EPS (non-GAAP): $17.28 in FY26 compared to $14.13 in FY25 (22% growth).

SEGMENT RESULTS OF OPERATIONS (in millions):
- Productivity and Business Processes: Revenue $139,996 (+16%), Cost of revenue $25,017, Operating expenses $31,100, Operating income $83,879 (+20%).
- Intelligent Cloud: Revenue $137,791 (+30%), Cost of revenue $57,876, Operating expenses $22,943, Operating income $56,972 (+28%).
- More Personal Computing: Revenue $54,052 (-1%), Cost of revenue $23,481, Operating expenses $16,185, Operating income $14,386 (+2%).

title: Microsoft FY2026 Annual Report - Note 1 Accounting Policies
section: Notes to Financial Statements - Note 1 Accounting Policies
text:
NOTES TO FINANCIAL STATEMENTS
NOTE 1 — ACCOUNTING POLICIES
Revenue Recognition:
When desktop applications and cloud services depend on a significant level of integration, interdependency, and interrelation such that the individual components are not distinct (such as Office 365), they are accounted for together as a single performance obligation, and revenue is recognized ratably over the period in which cloud services are provided.

OpenAI Strategic Partnership:
We have a long-term strategic partnership with OpenAI originally established in 2019 and extended in October 2025. We have an investment accounted for under the equity method that represents an approximate 25% interest on an as-converted basis.
For fiscal year 2026, we recorded revenue from commercial arrangements with OpenAI of $24.1 billion, and accounts receivable was $6.0 billion. In October 2025, OpenAI formed a public benefit corporation and completed a recapitalization ('OpenAI Recapitalization'). During fiscal year 2026, our proportionate ownership decreased and we recorded dilution gains in other income (expense), net.
